# ldn.lol — what's on in central London

> Listings and news for central London — zones 1 and 2, not the outer boroughs. Every entry names the source it came from and the day it was checked against it. Independent publication: not a government outlet, not a ticket seller, not affiliated with any venue.

How this site works, in five rules:

- **Every fact names where it came from, and when we last looked.** The source prints as text, never as a live link.
- **Nothing is listed on a date we could not confirm.** If the organiser said "early November" and nothing more, no invented day appears here — the missing day appears instead.
- **What's on, not what went wrong.** No politics, no crime, no tragedy.
- **We pick the best, and say why.** Picking out the best of something is the job; running a named business down is not.
- **A page exists when there is something to put on it.** No empty templates waiting for content.

## What a reader finds here

- [Events](https://ldn.lol/events/): events on dates confirmed with the organiser, with times, prices and running order where the organiser published them.
- [News](https://ldn.lol/news/): what changed in the city. Long pieces carrying the whole calendar or the whole figure, not a wire paragraph.
- [About](https://ldn.lol/about/): the rules above, written out at length.

## Where the facts come from

The organiser, or the publication that reported it: Time Out London, the Evening Standard, BBC London, Londonist, and the organisers themselves. Each entry prints that name and the date it was verified. Venue coordinates are geocoded once and stored in the data; where the geocoder returns the wrong place, the entry publishes without a map rather than with a wrong one.

Where a voice from Reddit appears in the text, it is a direct quotation from a public post, attributed to the subreddit rather than to the person.

What has not been announced is said to be unannounced. A closing date nobody has given, a theme not yet confirmed and a running order still to come are three things this site names rather than fills in.

## Events

- [Lord Mayor's Show 2026](https://ldn.lol/events/lord-mayors-show-2026/): Saturday 14 November, 11am, from Mansion House: an eight-century-old procession that closes almost the whole City of London and costs nothing to watch.
- [BFI London Film Festival 2026](https://ldn.lol/events/bfi-london-film-festival-2026/): Andrew Scott and Olivia Colman open the 70th LFF on 7 October in Elsinore. The festival runs to 18 October, and tickets go on general sale on 17 September.
- [London Design Festival 2026](https://ldn.lol/events/london-design-festival-2026/): Nine days, eleven design districts and a light installation inside St Paul's Cathedral. The 24th festival runs 12–20 September, and most of it is free to walk into.
- [Open House Festival 2026](https://ldn.lol/events/open-house-festival-2026/): For nine days in September, buildings across all 33 boroughs open their doors for free. The 35th edition runs 12–20 September, and the ticketed places went on sale in August.
- [Totally Thames 2026](https://ldn.lol/events/totally-thames-2026/): A month of art, performance and river adventures along the Thames through September — a film installation on Blackfriars Bridge, a dance duet in the Brunel tunnel shaft, an opera about water.
- [Notting Hill Carnival 2026](https://ldn.lol/events/notting-hill-carnival-2026/): Three days over the August bank holiday for Carnival's sixtieth year: Panorama on the Saturday, J'Ouvert and Children's Day on the Sunday, the main parade on the Monday. Free, and enormous.

## News

- [The Bayeux Tapestry is in England for the first time in 900 years](https://ldn.lol/news/bayeux-tapestry-at-the-british-museum/): Seventy metres of eleventh-century embroidery go on show from 10 September until 11 July 2027. Tickets are £33, and the next release is on 21 October.
- [A gallery closed to the public since 1943 reopens this month](https://ldn.lol/news/nature-and-us-opens-a-gallery-shut-since-1943/): The Natural History Museum's new free gallery puts a 400,000-year-old hand-axe beside a Star Wars toy that spent the 1980s under the sea.
- [The Fourth Plinth changes hands on 10 September](https://ldn.lol/news/lady-in-blue-takes-the-fourth-plinth/): Tschabalala Self's Lady in Blue goes up in Trafalgar Square from 10 September and stays until summer 2028 — the longest commitment in public art here.
- [Eleven artists are installing work in Regent's Park for free](https://ldn.lol/news/frieze-sculpture-in-regents-park/): From 16 September to 1 November, eleven artists take over the English Gardens on the theme of hybridity. No ticket, no booking, no queue.
- [Apple has created a job whose stated task is talking to governments](https://ldn.lol/news/apples-chairman-now-has-a-policy-job/): Tim Cook stopped being chief executive on 1 September. His new role comes with a remit Apple wrote down: engaging with policymakers around the world.
- [Venice opens the autumn, and a British film opens Venice](https://ldn.lol/news/venice-opens-the-autumn-with-a-british-film/): Danny Boyle's Ink starts the 83rd Mostra on 2 September. It is the first of the three festivals that decide what London's cinemas show in October.
- [The V&A closing dates worth putting in a diary](https://ldn.lol/news/va-exhibitions-closing-dates/): Four V&A exhibitions have published closing dates and one opens in November. Schiaparelli goes first, on 8 November — and it is the one with the shortest run left.
- [Notting Hill Carnival turns sixty](https://ldn.lol/news/notting-hill-carnival-turns-60/): A plaque at Westbourne Park names seventy people who built Carnival — unveiled for its sixtieth year, and for seventy years since London Transport went recruiting in the Caribbean.
- [A partial lunar eclipse, visible from London](https://ldn.lol/news/partial-lunar-eclipse-over-london/): London's second eclipse in a fortnight: 93% of the Moon in shadow at 5.12am on Friday 28 August, no glasses needed, and Parliament Hill the one obvious place to stand.
- [What is actually hanging in London right now](https://ldn.lol/news/ten-exhibitions-on-in-london/): Ten shows are on the critics' list. Six of them close before January, one has sold more advance tickets than anything in Tate's 128-year history, and two of the best are free.
